Parameterization in BayesIRTplot

Source: vignettes/articles/parameterization.Rmd
parameterization.Rmd

This article provides details on the parameterization of item response theory (IRT) models fitted in blavaan, and explains how those parameters are transformed and used for plotting in BayesIRTplot.

IRT models may be fitted under different parameterizations and metrics. To scale the latent response variable, two parameterizations may be used: 1) theta parameterization, in which the residual variance of the latent response variable is fixed to one, 2) delta parameterization, in which the total variance of the latent response variable is fixed to one (Kamata & Bauer, 2008). In addition, different link functions may be used to relate the latent trait to the probability of a correct response, including the probit link, which corresponds to the normal-ogive model, and the logit link, which corresponds to the logistic model.

The current version of BayesIRTplot supports unidimensional two-parameter IRT models for binary items. In blavaan, these models are fitted using the theta parameterization and a probit link (i.e., the normal-ogive model; Merkle, n.d.). blavaan provides posterior draws of item discrimination (aa) and item threshold (τ\tau) parameters. BayesIRTplot applies the following transformations and calculations:

  1. Under the normal-ogive model, the probability of a correct response (pp) is calculated as the probability that the underlying latent response (Y*Y^*) exceeds the item threshold (τ\tau):

    p=P(X=1∣θ)=P(Y*>τ∣θ)=Φ(aθ−τ), p = P(X = 1 \mid \theta) = P(Y^* > \tau\ \mid \theta) = \Phi(a\theta - \tau),

    Y*∣θ∼N(aθ,1) Y^* \mid\ \theta \sim N(a\theta, 1) where θ\theta is the latent trait and Φ(⋅)\Phi(\cdot) denotes the cumulative distribution function of the standard normal distribution.

  2. Item discrimination (aa) is then converted from the probit to the logit metric using

    alogit=1.702a a_{\text{logit}} = 1.702a and is reported under the logit metric.

  3. Item information (ii) is calculated as i=alogit2p(1−p) i = a_{\text{logit}}^2 p(1-p)

  4. Item threshold (τ\tau) is not transformed and is reported under the original probit metric.

References:

Merkle, E. C. (n.d.). Ordinal models in blavaan. blavaan. https://blavaan.org/articles/ordinal.html

Kamata, A., & Bauer, D. J. (2008). A Note on the Relation Between Factor Analytic and Item Response Theory Models. Structural Equation Modeling, 15(1), 136–153. https://doi.org/10.1080/10705510701758406
